title: A walk names a panel control in a way a rename cannot break
goal: Scripted walks find panel controls by the words printed on them, so the day a row is renamed or moves into another section, every walk that touched it fails and somebody spends a task repairing them. That bill was paid four separate times in the last day alone, and it lands on the feature work in focus, because building UI means editing that panel. Give a walk a way to name a control that survives its label changing.
notes:
Filed by the 2026-09-09 triage pass. This serves the ui-building focus by removing a tax that focus work pays: the panel is the file nearly every focus task edits.

The bill, from the last day of the queue: "Thirteen scripted walks still look for an Outline row that is now a Border", "Five stale walks still ask for the outline that moved into Effects", "Four walks cannot find the Shadow entry in the Effects list", "Four walks stop on a panel control that has scrolled out of reach", plus "Bring the scripted walks back in line with the split panel", which was dropped. Five tasks, one cause.

Not all of it is renaming: some of those were controls scrolled out of view, which is a different fix and already landed (reveal steps). What is left is the name.

See docs/design/playtest-harness.md and Scripts/playtest/. Worth checking whether the accessibility identifier already on these controls can be the stable name, since the harness reads the accessibility tree already.
acceptance: A walk can name a panel control by something that does not change when its words change, and at least the walks that broke this week use it
A control that has genuinely gone away still fails the walk loudly, so this does not turn a real break into a pass
Renaming one row in the panel and running the full set proves it: the walks that only knew the old word still pass
The change is written up where walk authors will read it, in the playtest harness design doc

log.note: Read the harness. A walk names a panel row by the words on it (playtestField(title)); PlaytestPanelPress.fields() hands those words to `narrow`, which is what `in:` matches. So `in` is pure product copy and a copy change breaks every walk that used it.

Adversarial review of the idea, before building. (1) Aliases rejected: keeping the old word alive means a retired row can drift onto a neighbour and a walk passes on the wrong control, which is exactly acceptance item 2. (2) A separate stable KEY is only steady if whoever edits the copy leaves it alone, so it must not be typed at the call site: it comes off the model (EffectKind.rawValue, LayerPartRow.id), where a copy edit physically cannot reach it. (3) Discoverability is the real risk -- an author writes what they see. Fix: the panel listing and every not-found failure print the steady name beside the word, so the first failure hands you the durable name. (4) Shortest version: only the two lists whose row words come from the model get steady names (Appearance parts, the Effects list). Width/Height/Layout are structural words that have not moved, and giving everything a key would be noise.

Built it. A row in Appearance and a row in the Effects list now carry a steady name beside their words, taken off the model (LayerEffectRow.steadyNames off EffectKind + ordinal, LayerPartRow.steadyNames off LayerPart/ColorSlot), and a walk writes it with a mark: in: "@border". PlaytestSteadyName in PhotonzCore owns the convention and is unit tested; the app layer carries it on PanelTargetView.steady and matches it in narrow(), pressTarget, panelTarget, panelScrollTarget, checkInView, openPanelMenu, the tooltip reading and the colour drag.

Adversarial review of the BUILT thing, on the real probe. (a) An author writes what they can see, so a `panel` step now prints the steady names beside every control -- Switch (Border, on, @border @border.1) -- and a step naming a row that is not there answers "the steady names on screen: @border, @border.1, @fill", paste-ready. Verified both by running throwaway walks. (b) The first cut put the steady names inside the joined detail string, which would have silently broken all 19 `in: "Border, Width"` steps, since that form is matched as a substring of that very string. Caught before running anything; steady names now travel in their own field and `in` splits on commas and asks for each piece separately, so `@border, Width` works and words and steady names may be mixed. (c) Naming a control by a steady name is rejected outright rather than falling through to press whatever sits in the row. (d) @fill.1 beside @fill was noise, since nothing in Appearance is countable: an uncounted part gets one name.

Proof for the rename. Changed EffectKind.border.title from "Border" to "Outline", rebuilt the probe, ran the twenty converted walks: seventeen passed, the three that did not had failed identically at baseline. Ran border-offset-walk.json, left naming the row by its word, and it failed: 'no menu called "Border" is in the window'. Then put the title back and re-ran: same seventeen green.

Proof that a real break is still a break. A walk asking for `in: "@glow"` on a layer with no glow fails with 'no row called "@glow" is in the panel, so there is nothing on it to press; the steady names on screen: @border, @border.1, @fill'. It does not drift onto the Border switch that IS on screen. That is why this is a steady name and not an alias: keeping the old word alive would have let a retired row answer for its neighbour.

Twenty walks converted -- the ones repaired by 202256d8 (fifteen walks) and deb5d9d2 (five walks), which are the walks the Outline-to-Border rename broke. Also converted their reads claims, which quoted the row word, and their panelMenu/dragColor/rightClick row names.

Not done, on purpose: the rows of an ordinary menu still go by their words, the plus menu in Effects being the one exception (choose: "@border"), because that menu is built off the same model the rows are. Giving every menu item in the app a durable id is a different job. Also left alone: Width, Height, Layout, Position & Size -- structural words that have not moved.
Ran only the walks I touched (20) plus two throwaway ones, never the full sweep. Asked for a sweep with queue/bin/sweep.sh request. Scripts/test.sh green, 5705 tests.

Three of the twenty still fail and failed the same way at baseline before any of this: border-effect, glow-effect, label-fills-a-row each stop on a control the dock has scrolled out of reach. Filed with the commands and output as three-walks-stop-on-a-panel-control-the-dock-has (p2-normal).

Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-12-steady-panel-names.json, with a real screen capture (Grants said the probe had Screen Recording). Written up for walk authors in docs/design/playtest-harness.md, 'A row of the panel has a second name that a rename cannot touch'.
